findings.issue_text: Permission gate uses AND (`&&`) where OR (`||`) is intended in `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, requiring users to be both admin and owner instead of either, blocking team admins from adding guests
Calendar update uses the caller's credentials (`ctx.user`) instead of the organizer's credentials, causing calendar updates to silently fail or error for non-organizer callers

Case-sensitivity mismatch in dedup and blacklist filtering: blacklist emails are lowercased but compared against original-case guest emails, allowing blacklisted guests to bypass filtering and enabling duplicate attendees with different casing
Errors from `sendAddGuestsEmails` are swallowed: the caught error is never logged and the handler still returns a success message, masking real email delivery failures
`isInvalidEmail` flag is never cleared on success, in `onChange`, or on dialog reopen, causing a stale validation error message to persist

Initial state `[""]` for `multiEmailValue` triggers a misleading "Emails must be unique and valid" error when the user submits without entering anything, and allows duplicates of the empty string placeholder
Authorization logic uses `&&` instead of `||` in `isTeamAdminOrOwner` check, requiring user to be both admin AND owner instead of either
Any booking attendee (including external users) is authorized to add unlimited guests to the organizer's booking/calendar event, exposing event details and enabling spam
EventManager is built from the requesting user's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's (booking.user), causing calendar updates to fail silently or target the wrong account
No `.max()` on the guests array schema, allowing unlimited guests per request and enabling mass email spam, calendar API quota exhaustion, and DB load
Duplicate attendee check is case-sensitive while blacklist check is lowercased, allowing users to bypass the duplicate filter by varying email casing
No validation of booking status (e.g., CANCELLED/REJECTED) or whether the booking time has passed, allowing guests and calendar updates to be added to stale or cancelled bookings

Unbounded `guests` array in `addGuests.schema.ts` — no `.max()` length cap on the Zod array schema, allowing a single request to fan out into unbounded DB inserts, emails, translation loads, and calendar API calls
Email fan-out in `sendAddGuestsEmails` scales with the entire attendee list rather than just new guests, and fires all emails concurrently via `Promise.all` without batching or throttling

N+1 `getTranslation` per attendee in `addGuests.handler.ts` — one `getTranslation` invocation per attendee inside a `.map`; should compute the set of unique locales first and load each translation once

Redundant attendees materialization on the read path — initial `prisma.booking.findFirst` includes `attendees: true` but the subsequent `prisma.booking.update` re-fetches the full attendee set; the first query's attendees load is mostly redundant

Partial failure: DB is committed before calendar update with no rollback, leaving inconsistent state that prevents user retry
No server-side deduplication within the guests array, allowing duplicate attendee records via direct API call bypassing client validation
`isInvalidEmail` is not reset to `false` on successful submission, leaving a stale error banner visible when the dialog is reopened

`replyTo` header leaks all attendee emails to all recipients, exposing attendee PII to unauthorized team members

Missing `team` field in CalendarEvent object causes team member notification loop to be silently skipped, so team members receive no notification when guests are added

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission gate uses AND (`&&`) where OR (`||`) is intended in `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, requiring users to be both admin and owner instead of either, blocking team admins from adding guests
Calendar update uses the caller's credentials (`ctx.user`) instead of the organizer's credentials, causing calendar updates to silently fail or error for non-organizer callers

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar sync is performed with an `EventManager` created from the *caller* (`const { user } = ctx;` and `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` then `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`). However, the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to call it (`isTeamAdminOrOwner` / `isAttendee` / `isOrganizer`). For attendee/admin callers, `ctx.user` may not have the organizer’s calendar credentials, even though the booking’s organizer user (and their `credentials`) is loaded via `include: { user: { ... credentials: true } }` and then ignored. This makes `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` likely to fail or no-op for non-organizer callers, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitivity mismatch in dedup and blacklist filtering: blacklist emails are lowercased but compared against original-case guest emails, allowing blacklisted guests to bypass filtering and enabling duplicate attendees with different casing
Errors from `sendAddGuestsEmails` are swallowed: the caught error is never logged and the handler still returns a success message, masking real email delivery failures

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not rethrow or otherwise signal failure. The handler then proceeds to `return { message: "Guests added" }` regardless of whether email sending failed. This masks real email delivery failures (and logs no error details). The proposed finding is directionally correct, though it’s slightly inaccurate to say the error is “never logged” since a generic message is logged without the error object.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isInvalidEmail` flag is never cleared on success, in `onChange`, or on dialog reopen, causing a stale validation error message to persist

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). In the success path (`addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`), the dialog is closed and `multiEmailValue` is reset, but `isInvalidEmail` is not cleared. Also, `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` does not reset `isInvalidEmail` on close/reopen. This can leave the validation error message visible on subsequent opens (stale state).

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same root problem: initializing the emails array as [" "] (an empty-string placeholder) causes validation/UX issues (e.g., invalid/unique errors) and should instead be an empty array with proper empty-state handling in the component.

matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same authorization bug: using `&&` in the team admin/owner permission check incorrectly requires both roles, and it should be `||` to allow either admin or owner.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any booking attendee (including external users) is authorized to add unlimited guests to the organizer's booking/calendar event, exposing event details and enabling spam

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly authorizes any logged-in user whose email matches a booking attendee (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then allows the mutation if `isAttendee` is true). There is no further restriction (e.g., organizer-only, admin-only, max guest count, rate limiting, domain allowlist), and the input schema is just `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no length bound. The handler then persists the new attendees (`createMany`) and updates the organizer’s calendar attendees (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`), and sends emails to attendees/new guests. This makes it verifiable from the diff that any attendee account can add an arbitrary number of guests to the event, which can be abused to spam or disclose event details to third parties.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built from the requesting user's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's (booking.user), causing calendar updates to fail silently or target the wrong account

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the booking organizer is fetched (organizer) and the booking query includes booking.user.credentials, but the calendar update uses `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...] })` where `user` is the requesting session user, not `booking.user`/organizer. Since this mutation allows non-organizers (team admin/owner or even an attendee) to call it, the calendar update (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`) will run with the wrong identity/credentials and can update the wrong account or fail when the requester lacks the organizer’s calendar credentials. This mismatch is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No `.max()` on the guests array schema, allowing unlimited guests per request and enabling mass email spam, calendar API quota exhaustion, and DB load

adjudication.rationale: The new server-side input validation in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (and the UI `MultiEmail` allows adding arbitrary entries). The handler then uses `createMany` to insert all provided guests and triggers calendar updates and email sending (`sendAddGuestsEmails`), so an authenticated caller could submit an excessively large array in a single request, causing high DB writes and outbound email/calendar operations. This is a verifiable missing bound in the diff with clear potential for abuse/load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate attendee check is case-sensitive while blacklist check is lowercased, allowing users to bypass the duplicate filter by varying email casing

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, duplicate filtering uses strict equality `guest === attendee.email` without normalizing case, while the blacklist list is lowercased (`.map(email => email.toLowerCase())`) but checked via `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`. This allows adding an email that differs only by casing from an existing attendee (bypassing the duplicate filter) and similarly can bypass the blacklist by changing casing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation of booking status (e.g., CANCELLED/REJECTED) or whether the booking time has passed, allowing guests and calendar updates to be added to stale or cancelled bookings

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation/handler updates `booking.attendees` and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` for any found booking after only doing a permission check. In `addGuests.handler.ts` there is no check of any booking state/status (e.g., cancelled/rejected) and no check that `startTime/endTime` are still in the future before mutating DB attendees and pushing calendar/email updates. This means stale/cancelled/past bookings (if such states exist in the booking model, which is typical) would still be modifiable and trigger calendar updates/emails, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded `guests` array in `addGuests.schema.ts` — no `.max()` length cap on the Zod array schema, allowing a single request to fan out into unbounded DB inserts, emails, translation loads, and calendar API calls

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new TRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests` whose input schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts`) allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code iterates over the resulting attendees to (1) `createMany` DB inserts for all provided guests, (2) load translations per attendee via `getTranslation` in a `map`, (3) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and (4) send emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails`, which maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` to enqueue email sends. Because there is no `.max()` (or other cap) in the schema, a single request can cause arbitrarily large fan-out work proportional to the array size, which is a real, verifiable risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email fan-out in `sendAddGuestsEmails` scales with the entire attendee list rather than just new guests, and fires all emails concurrently via `Promise.all` without batching or throttling

N+1 `getTranslation` per attendee in `addGuests.handler.ts` — one `getTranslation` invocation per attendee inside a `.map`; should compute the set of unique locales first and load each translation once

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `attendeesListPromises` is created by mapping over `bookingAttendees.attendees` and for each attendee it does `translate: await getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")`. This results in one `getTranslation` call per attendee, even when many attendees share the same locale (e.g., all `en`). That is a verifiable per-attendee repeated lookup pattern (an N+1-style performance inefficiency) that could be avoided by deduping locales and loading translations once per locale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant attendees materialization on the read path — initial `prisma.booking.findFirst` includes `attendees: true` but the subsequent `prisma.booking.update` re-fetches the full attendee set; the first query's attendees load is mostly redundant

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the initial prisma.booking.findFirst({ include: { attendees: true, ... }}) is not redundant: booking.attendees is used for permission checking (isAttendee) and to filter out already-invited emails when computing uniqueGuests. The later prisma.booking.update({ include: { attendees: true }, ... }) is used to obtain the updated attendee list for building attendeesList and updating calendars/emails. While there is some duplicated data fetching, it’s a potential optimization rather than a clear defect, and the proposed finding mischaracterizes the first attendees load as “mostly redundant.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: O(n × m) duplicate-email scan using nested loop with `.some()` in the `uniqueGuests` filter — should build a `Set` of existing attendee emails for O(1) lookups
`newGuests.includes(...)` inside the attendee email map in `sendAddGuestsEmails` is an O(attendees × newGuests) linear scan — should convert `newGuests` to a `Set` before the map

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the code does `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` inside `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`, which is indeed O(attendees × newGuests) due to a linear scan per attendee. However, this is a minor micro-optimization/performance nit rather than a clear defect/bug/security/correctness problem introduced by the diff; attendee/guest counts are typically small and nothing in the diff indicates this would be a practical issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zod schema with `.refine` callback is reconstructed on every render of the `AddGuestsDialog` component — should be moved to module scope to avoid per-render allocation

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(...).refine(...)` is indeed created inside the component body, so it will be reallocated on each render. However, this is a minor performance micro-optimization concern rather than a clear bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff. The code will function correctly as written, and the per-render allocation is unlikely to be considered a real review problem under the provided strict criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check uses `&&` instead of `||` in `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, requiring a user to be both admin AND owner instead of either one

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that check, which is inconsistent with the variable name and typical authorization intent (admin OR owner). As a result, a user who is only an admin (or only an owner) would fail the permission check and be forbidden unless they are also the organizer/attendee, making this a real correctness/authorization bug introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager uses requester's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, causing calendar updates to fail or hit the wrong account

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (`isAttendee` or `isTeamAdminOrOwner`). However, it builds the `EventManager` using the requester (`const { user } = ctx; ... const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });`) and then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. If the requester is an attendee or team member, this will use their OAuth/calendar credentials rather than the booking organizer’s, which can cause the calendar attendee update to fail (no credentials / wrong provider) or apply to the wrong connected account. The organizer’s identity is fetched separately (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) but is not used to fetch credentials or construct the `EventManager`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is called with the original `guests` array instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees to receive re-invite emails instead of guest-added notifications

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server filters input `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted ones) and only persists `uniqueGuests`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original, unfiltered array. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Therefore, if the caller includes an email that was already an attendee (and thus removed from `uniqueGuests`), that existing attendee will still match `includes(...)` and receive the “scheduled” email (i.e., a re-invite) instead of the “guests added” notification. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid this mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive duplicate and blacklist comparison for guest emails — `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guest` is compared verbatim, allowing mixed-case emails to bypass the blacklist
Server tRPC input schema for `guests` does not enforce uniqueness, unlike the client dialog, allowing duplicate submissions that may create duplicate attendee rows or throw a unique-constraint error
`onError` fallback to `unable_to_add_guests` toast is unreachable because template-string interpolation always yields a non-empty string

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the `onError` handler builds `message` using a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. Template literal interpolation always produces a string, and even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined`/empty and `t(err.message)` is empty, the result is still a non-empty string like `"undefined: "` or `": "`, which is truthy. Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will always use `message` and the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is effectively unreachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error in `sendAddGuestsEmails` catch block is captured but never logged, silently dropping mail-delivery failures without stack/code for debugging

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a try/catch around `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`. The `catch (err)` block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log/emit `err` (no stack trace, message, or code), effectively swallowing actionable failure details. While the finding misattributes the catch block to `sendAddGuestsEmails` (it’s actually in the handler), the underlying issue—mail-delivery failures being silently dropped without useful debugging info—is real and directly verifiable in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `<label htmlFor="emails">` in `MultiEmail.tsx` does not match any input id, breaking label focus and screen-reader association

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the label is rendered as `<label htmlFor="emails">`, but none of the rendered inputs (`<EmailField ... />`) are given an `id="emails"` (or any `id` prop at all) in this diff. Additionally, multiple `EmailField`s can be rendered in a list, so a single shared `htmlFor` would not correctly associate with a specific input anyway. This breaks the expected label-to-control association for focus and assistive technologies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hard-coded English response string `"Guests added"` is returned without translation, leaking English to non-web callers

adjudication.rationale: The handler `addGuestsHandler` does return `{ message: "Guests added" }`, which is a hard-coded English string. However, nothing in the diff shows any consumer using this return value for user-facing text; the web UI shows a toast using `t("guests_added")` on success and ignores the mutation response. Also, API responses are typically not localized, so calling this a “real” leak/bug is speculative beyond what’s verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` (AND) instead of `||` (OR), requiring the user to be both a team admin and a team owner instead of either one

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which means the flag is only true if the user is BOTH a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and the subsequent authorization gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, this would incorrectly deny access to users who are admins but not owners (or vice versa) unless they are also the organizer/attendee. This is a concrete, verifiable logic/authorization defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager initialized with the requesting user's credentials instead of the organizer's, causing calendar updates to fail silently when non-organizers add guests
No rollback if calendar update fails after DB write, and retry is permanently stuck because already-added guests are filtered out causing a misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error

adjudication.rationale: In addGuestsHandler, the DB is updated first (prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany). After that it calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) without any transaction/rollback or try/catch. If that calendar update throws, the mutation fails but the guests remain persisted in DB. On a retry with the same guest emails, the handler refetches the booking including attendees, filters out already-present emails via uniqueGuests, and if none remain it throws BAD_REQUEST with message "emails_must_be_unique_valid". That blocks retrying to repair the external calendar update and the error is misleading (emails may be valid/unique; they’re just already added).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` error is silently swallowed without logging the error object, and the handler returns success even when notification emails fail

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in a `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` block. The caught `err` is not logged or rethrown, so failures lose diagnostic detail and do not affect the mutation result. The handler proceeds to `return { message: "Guests added" };` even if email notifications fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is called with raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees to receive full 'You're scheduled' emails instead of 'new guests added' notifications

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted ones) and only persists `uniqueGuests` to the booking. However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw `guests` input, not `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` list controls whether each attendee gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (if their email is included) vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (otherwise). If the caller includes an email that is already an attendee in `guests` (the server schema does not prevent this), that existing attendee will be incorrectly classified as “new” and will receive the full scheduled email instead of the add-guests notification. Using `uniqueGuests` would avoid this misclassification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema does not validate email uniqueness within the input array, allowing duplicate emails that could cause DB constraint violations or duplicate attendee records
`isInvalidEmail` is never cleared to false when validation succeeds on retry, causing stale error message to display alongside server errors

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails in `handleAdd`, but it is never reset to `false` when validation later succeeds. On a retry where the user fixes the emails and `safeParse` passes, the mutation is triggered without clearing `isInvalidEmail`, so the inline "Emails must be unique and valid" error can remain visible even though inputs are now valid (and even if the server returns an error toast). It’s only cleared on Cancel, not on successful local validation or mutation callbacks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client and server both define ZAddGuestsInputSchema with the same name but divergent behavior — client adds a uniqueness refinement the server lacks, risking silent contract drift

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces two different `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` definitions with the same identifier but different shapes/validation:
- Client (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx`) defines `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` as `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` to enforce uniqueness.
- Server (`addGuests.schema.ts`) defines `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` as an object `{ bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email()) }` with no uniqueness refinement.

This is verifiable drift: the server does not validate uniqueness of `guests` (and the handler’s `uniqueGuests` filter does not dedupe duplicates within the submitted `guests` array), so a caller bypassing the UI could submit duplicate emails and the server would accept them (potentially causing duplicate attendee creation attempts / inconsistent behavior). The shared name makes this easier to miss during maintenance, increasing contract drift risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail flag is never reset when user edits the email field after a validation failure, leaving a stale error banner visible

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd()`, which shows the red error banner. However, `isInvalidEmail` is only reset in the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). The `MultiEmail` field updates `multiEmailValue` via `setMultiEmailValue`, but no code resets `isInvalidEmail` when the user edits the email inputs (or when validation later succeeds). This leaves the error banner potentially stale/visible after the user fixes the input until they cancel/close (or submit successfully and the dialog closes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead fallback in error toast: template literal always produces non-empty string, so the fallback message can never be reached

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the error handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always returns a string; even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` and/or `t(err.message)` is falsy, `message` becomes something like `"undefined: "`, which is still truthy. Therefore the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never be used, making it dead/unreachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded English string "Guests added" in handler return value bypasses i18n while the rest of the flow uses translation functions

adjudication.rationale: The handler does return a hardcoded English string (`return { message: "Guests added" };` in `addGuests.handler.ts`). However, in the diff the only shown consumer (`AddGuestsDialog`) does not use this return value for UI/i18n—it shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` on success. Since the response message is not demonstrated to be user-facing or translated elsewhere, this is an inconsistency/nit rather than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email sending error is silently swallowed with console.log instead of the project's structured logger, making failures invisible in production

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that does not rethrow or return an error, and it logs only `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging the actual error object. This means email-send failures are effectively swallowed (the mutation still returns success), and the only signal is an unstructured console message, reducing visibility/debuggability in production.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ZAddGuestsInputSchema is recreated inside the component body on every render instead of being hoisted to module scope

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is indeed defined inside the `AddGuestsDialog` component and will be recreated on each render. However, this is not a bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff; it’s at most a minor performance/style optimization concern. Nothing in the diff shows this causing incorrect behavior or a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner variable name implies OR logic but the code uses AND, incorrectly denying plain team admins

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with AND logic:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This requires a user to be *both* a team admin and a team owner to pass the team-based permission check. Given the variable name and typical role semantics (“admin OR owner”), this will deny access to plain team admins (and possibly everyone except owners, depending on how `isTeamAdmin` treats owners). The subsequent permission gate uses `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...`, so this directly affects authorization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Initial state [""] contradicts the length === 0 guard — a single empty-string row is not caught by the length check

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `multiEmailValue` is initialized to `[""]`. In `handleAdd`, the early return only triggers when `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, which will not catch the initial state (length is 1). As a result, clicking “Add” with the untouched initial empty row falls through to validation, fails `z.string().email()`, and sets `isInvalidEmail` instead of being treated as “no emails provided.” This makes the length guard ineffective for the default state, which is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail component mutates its value prop with `value = value || []` instead of using a local const

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the line `value = value || []` only reassigns the local function parameter variable; it does not mutate the caller’s prop or the underlying array. Given the prop type `value: string[]`, `value` shouldn’t be `undefined` anyway, making this primarily an unnecessary/cleanup/style issue (and possibly a lint preference like no-param-reassign), not a verifiable correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reusing AttendeeScheduledEmail for new-guest notification couples two distinct user-facing narratives to one template, risking unintended drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally reuses the existing Scheduled email templates by creating thin wrappers (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail/OrganizerAddGuestsEmail) that set different i18n keys (title/subject) while leveraging the same base layout/content. The proposed finding (“risking unintended drift”) is a speculative design concern about future maintainability, not a concrete, verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness) introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BookingListItem action id "add_members" mismatches the label "additional_guests" — members and guests are different concepts in the codebase

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the action entry uses id: "add_members" but the UI label is correctly driven by t("additional_guests"). The id appears to be an internal identifier (and is even reused as a data-testid on the dialog button), and there is no logic shown that depends on the id matching the label’s concept. This is a naming consistency nit, not a verifiable bug or defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization check uses `&&` instead of `||` for `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, requiring user to be both admin and owner rather than either

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The name and typical authorization semantics imply it should be an OR check (admin OR owner). As written, team admins who are not owners (a common role split) would be incorrectly denied by the subsequent `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` permission gate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist bypass via case-sensitive comparison: blacklist emails are lowercased but `guest` is compared as-is, allowing case-variant emails to bypass the blacklist
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same vulnerability: the blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is not, so a case-sensitive `includes` check can be bypassed using uppercase/lowercase variants.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw `guests` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of filtered `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees to receive the wrong email template
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core bug: `sendAddGuestsEmails` decides which template to send by checking whether an attendee email is in the "new guests" list, but the list being used/passed (`guests` instead of a filtered `uniqueGuests`/actual new additions) can include existing attendees. This causes existing attendees to be misclassified and receive the wrong email template.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial failure: DB is committed before calendar update with no rollback, leaving inconsistent state that prevents user retry

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. There is no transaction/rollback or compensating logic if the calendar update throws. Because the DB now already contains the new attendees, a user retrying the mutation will hit `uniqueGuests.length === 0` (since the guests are now present in `booking.attendees`) and the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`), effectively preventing retry and leaving the external calendar potentially out of sync with the DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side deduplication within the guests array, allowing duplicate attendee records via direct API call bypassing client validation
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the lack of deduplication within the submitted guests/input array, which can result in duplicate attendee records being inserted (e.g., via createMany) if repeated emails are provided, especially when bypassing client-side validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isInvalidEmail` is not reset to `false` on successful submission, leaving a stale error banner visible when the dialog is reopened

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation in `handleAdd`, but in the mutation `onSuccess` handler it only calls `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and `setMultiEmailValue([""])` and never resets `isInvalidEmail` to `false`. Because the dialog component remains mounted (it’s always rendered in `BookingListItem` and only `open` toggles), closing and reopening the dialog will preserve `isInvalidEmail === true`, keeping the error banner visible even after a successful submission/reopen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-sending errors are silently swallowed: `err` object is not logged and user receives a success toast despite email failure

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which neither logs the actual `err` nor fails the mutation. The handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the client `onSuccess` runs and shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` even if email sending failed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive attendee authorization check: differing email casing between `user.email` and stored attendee email denies legitimate attendees and allows case-variant duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, attendee authorization uses a strict case-sensitive comparison: `booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)`. If the stored attendee email differs only by casing from `user.email`, a legitimate attendee could be treated as not an attendee and be denied unless they are organizer/admin. Similarly, duplicate prevention for new guests is also case-sensitive: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, so adding `A@ex.com` when `a@ex.com` already exists will not be filtered out and can create case-variant duplicates. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff and is a correctness/security issue (authorization + duplicate handling) tied to email normalization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `replyTo` header leaks all attendee emails to all recipients, exposing attendee PII to unauthorized team members

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the email payload sets `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. This includes *all attendee emails* in the Reply-To header. The same template is sent not only to the organizer but also to each `teamMember` (`toAddresses = [this.teamMember?.email || this.calEvent.organizer.email]` and the email-manager loops over `calendarEvent.team.members`). As a result, any recipient of this organizer/team email can see the full attendee email list in the headers, which is a verifiable PII exposure introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer email subject uses `attendees[0].name` which may be empty for newly added guests, rendering an empty name in the subject and crashing if `attendees` is empty

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the subject interpolates `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. In the new add-guests flow (`addGuests.handler.ts`), newly added guests are created with `name: ""`, so it’s plausible the first attendee in `calEvent.attendees` has an empty name, producing an email subject with a blank name. However, the diff does not clearly demonstrate that `attendees` can be empty at this point (the handler adds at least one guest before sending), so the “crashing if attendees is empty” part is not strictly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing `team` field in CalendarEvent object causes team member notification loop to be silently skipped, so team members receive no notification when guests are added

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, team member notifications are only sent inside `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }`. But the `CalendarEvent` object constructed in `addGuests.handler.ts` (`const evt: CalendarEvent = { ... }`) does not include any `team` field at all, and the booking query only includes `eventType: true` (not `eventType.team`/members). As a result, after `formatCalEvent(calEvent)`, `calendarEvent.team` will be undefined (or at least cannot contain members from this handler), so the loop that emails team members will be skipped and only the organizer email will be sent.
